summary:
Acre is a state of Brazil and stands under Brazil's national framework, whose provisions are carried in the country-level assessment. Within Acre, the state legislature, the Rio Branco city council and the state courts have added their own enforceable instruments covering discrimination, social name use and document rectification, administered by state and municipal bodies.

State Decree 7311 of 3 August 2017 created a State Council for Combating Discrimination and Promoting the Rights of Lesbians, Gays, Bisexuals, Travestis and Transsexuals, charged with proposing public policy for LGBTQ people in Acre.

Acre State Law 3355 of 18 December 2017, published 19 December 2017 and in force 60 days after publication, guarantees every natural person the use of their social name before the state's direct and indirect public administration. State servants must address the person by the indicated name in written acts, both the civil-registry name and the social name appear on formal documents such as official letters and summonses, pejorative expressions are prohibited, and non-compliance is treated as a functional infraction carrying administrative liability.

Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is independently prohibited in the state capital by Rio Branco Law 2389, enacted 30 December 2020 and in force on publication on 5 January 2021. The ordinance reaches refusal of entry or stay in any public or private establishment open to the public, selective service not required by law, denial or surcharge on hotel or pension lodging, denial or surcharge on rental, purchase or lending of movable or immovable property, restriction of access to buses and taxis, denial of school enrollment and incitement to discrimination or violence through any medium. Penalties run from warning through a fine set by municipal regulation, suspension of activities or an operating licence for up to 30 days, and interdiction or revocation graded by gravity, recidivism and economic capacity; liability applies to individuals and to for-profit and non-profit legal entities, complaints may be filed by any resident, and confidentiality is guaranteed on request.

Document rectification is supported by Court of Justice of Acre Order 15/2024, published 15 October 2024, which establishes that legal change of name and gender on documents must be free of charge for individuals lacking financial means. In 2025 Ariel Sebastos Nascimento Silva, a Sena Madureira native, became the first person in Acre to obtain a civil-registry rectification to a non-binary sex entry, granted by judge Luana Cláudia de Albuquerque Campos after a two-year process run through the Defensoria Pública do Estado do Acre; the compliance order to the Sena Madureira registry was still awaiting transfer and no physical rectified documents had issued as of late June 2025. Non-binary marker changes continue to require judicial action case by case.

State service access rests on a Technical Cooperation Agreement signed on 29 January 2025 between the State Secretariat for Social Assistance and Human Rights and the Public Prosecutor's Office of Acre, which accompanied the launch of a booklet guiding trans and travesti people through name and gender rectification and through health, education, employment and non-discriminatory care. The agreement assigns the Public Prosecutor's Office oversight of public policy enforcement and of essential services including the trans outpatient clinic. State authorities recorded no trans deaths in Acre in 2024.

Between 2007 and 2018 the Associação de Homossexuais do Acre recorded 18 murders of homosexual people in the state, 14 of them in Rio Branco. Those are raw counts reported by a single association, with no population denominator, so they cannot be read as a per-capita rate or compared directly with other states.

Local hostility has surfaced in the legislature. On 13 November 2024 the Rio Branco City Council approved Bill 14/2024 by 10 votes to 1 to prohibit the participation of children and adolescents in LGBTQ pride parades; the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office criticised the bill for perpetuating stereotypes about homosexual people, and Mayor Tião Bocalom vetoed it as unconstitutional.
tangentialFactors:
Analysts assessing Brazilian LGBTQ+ protections describe them as among the most progressive in Latin America on paper while reporting uneven enforcement in practice: larger cities with established legal infrastructure are broadly welcoming, whereas smaller cities and rural areas, expressly including those in Acre, may present more social friction despite identical legal rights.

Acre's own courts have produced adoption precedent earlier than the national framework: on 30 May 2008 a ruling in Senador Guiomard permitted a gay couple in an eight-year stable relationship to adopt.

State-level protections in Acre are layered rather than substitutive. The state council, the state social-name law and the capital-city discrimination ordinance each operate alongside the national provisions, so a complaint in Rio Branco can be brought under municipal ordinance as well as under national law, while conduct outside the capital falls to state and national instruments alone.
localsOnly:
Law 3355 obliges state servants to undergo training in the social-name rules, requires the State Secretariat of Justice and Human Rights to disseminate the law, restricts use of the civil-registry name to internal administrative purposes alongside the social name, and exposes non-compliant servants to administrative liability as a functional infraction.

Order 15/2024 removes cost as a barrier to name and gender rectification for Acre residents who lack financial means, and the Public Prosecutor's Office of Acre holds oversight of enforcement under the January 2025 cooperation agreement.

The state public defender's office and the State Secretariat for Social Assistance and Human Rights ran a name-and-gender rectification clinic on 28 June 2025 from 8h to 13h at the Defensoria, requiring RG and CPF, passport where held, voter title, proof of address and negative certificates covering state, federal, electoral, labour and military service for those registered as male, alongside health, social and electoral services.

Identified barriers for Acre residents include exclusion from dignified work driven by prejudice, with many people having no fixed income and depending on social programmes, and school dropout limiting progression to higher education.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 18 murders recorded between 2007 and 2018 are raw counts from one association with no population denominator supplied; a per-capita rate for Acre, and any comparison with other states or with national totals, remains unresolved on this inventory.

The non-binary registry ruling issued in 2025 had not yet produced physical documents as of late June 2025, and whether other Acre residents obtain a non-binary marker without litigation is not sourced.

Complaint volumes, sanctions imposed and outcomes under Rio Branco Law 2389 are not sourced; no enforcement record for the ordinance appears in the inventory.

Whether municipalities in Acre other than Rio Branco have adopted anti-discrimination ordinances is not sourced.

The subsequent activity and current composition of the council created by Decree 7311 are not sourced beyond its establishment in 2017.

Capacity, hours and waiting times at the trans outpatient clinic referenced in the January 2025 cooperation agreement are not sourced.

Whether the training and dissemination duties assigned to the State Secretariat of Justice and Human Rights under Law 3355 have been carried out, and any disciplinary cases under the law, are not sourced.
